# #1598: Patch: a lost keyword leaves the board looking like a loss, not a gain
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

When an effect strips a keyword off a unit — Taunt knocked off an unbreakable defender, say — the board today pops the keyword icon in, plays its 'you gained a keyword' particles and the buff sound: exactly the show it puts on for gaining one. After the fix a loss reads as a loss: the icon leaves, the particles point down, and the sound is the debuff one — the way the game log already says 'lost'.

## Why

The `keywordGranted` event's `lost` flag is ignored by all three presentation layers: the animation row plays `jk-icon-pop` unconditionally (`apps/web/src/game/animations.ts:337-342`; a literal pop-in, `animations.css:1010-1014`), the FX recipe returns the grant recipe (`apps/web/src/fx/cues.ts:740-753`), and the cue plays `sfx("buff")` unconditionally (`apps/web/src/audio/cues.ts:517`) — while `buffed` right above shows the intended polarity (`:513-516`, buff vs debuff by sign). The design doc names this an open seam (`docs/polish/4-edge-cases.md:1664-1674` and its Known-limits entry at `:1771`), and BUILD M5-T4's row still reads only 'icon present'. The game log is the only layer that handles it (`apps/web/src/game/Log.tsx:318`).

## Proposal

Add the removal variant: a `data-lost` marker on the `data-animating` target (the `positionSwitched` `[data-position="DEF"]` selector at `animations.css:1160-1168` is the precedent) with a pop-out keyframe; a `lost` branch in the `keyword` FX recipe (downward/void cue); `sfx("debuff")` when `event.lost`; and BUILD.md's `keywordGranted` row gains the `lost` case.

## Where it lands

`apps/web/src/game/animations.{ts,css}`, `apps/web/src/fx/cues.ts`, `apps/web/src/audio/cues.ts` and their test files; `BUILD.md`. Spec R46.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Feeding `keywordGranted` with `lost: true` produces the removal animation variant (not `jk-icon-pop`), a debuff/void FX cue, and `sfx("debuff")` — asserted in the animation, FX and audio tests.
- [ ] Ordinary grants unchanged; `prefers-reduced-motion` still drains synchronously.
- [ ] The wire type's `lost?: true` (generated) is only read, never edited.

## Size and risks

Small-medium, client-only, no wire or engine change. Low risk — every mechanism already has a polarity precedent on the same table rows.
